question: Why do vector databases not use a cross-encoder for the whole search instead of embeddings?
options: Cross-encoders are less accurate than embeddings
A cross-encoder must read the query together with every document at query time, which is far too slow for a whole corpus; embeddings are computed once per document
explanation: Bi-encoders (embeddings) trade accuracy for precomputation. The usual design retrieves candidates fast, then reranks a few dozen with the slower, more accurate model.

question: The reranker returns `Sure! Here are the scores: {"scores": [{"id": "doc-9", "score": 10}]}`, but doc-9 was not among the candidates. What should the pipeline do?
options: Ignore the invented id and keep the candidates in retrieval order (or by any valid scores)
Fetch doc-9 and put it first
Throw an error so the user retries
Retry until the model stops inventing ids
explanation: Only candidates you sent can be ranked. Invented ids and invalid scores are ignored; missing scores fall back to retrieval order, so the worst case is no reranking, not an error.

question: In a chat, a user asks "What does the Scale plan include?" and then "And can I get a refund on it?". Which query-side technique matters most for the second message?
options: Rewriting the follow-up into a standalone question using the conversation ("Can I get a refund on the Scale plan?")
explanation: "it" means nothing to a retriever. Conversational query rewriting resolves references before the search.

question: A team adds multi-query (one extra model call) and HyDE (another call) to every search. What must they check before shipping?
options: Nothing: more model calls always improve quality
That the model never returns malformed JSON
That HyDE passages are shown to users as answers
That recall on the golden set improves enough to justify the added latency and cost of two calls per request, and that failures fall back to the original question
explanation: Query-side steps run before the search on every request. Measure the gain, budget the latency, and make every failure degrade to plain retrieval.
